title: Finite-type Proj is proper over its degree-zero spectrum
statement: Let $A=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}A_n$ be a commutative nonnegatively graded ring. If $A$ is a finite type $A_0$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], then the structural morphism $\operatorname{Proj}(A)\to\operatorname{Spec}(A_0)$ [def-pc-proj, def-weil-affine-spectrum] is proper [def-weil-proper-morphism].

from.place: Proof Step 3: dimension-normalized Verdier duality, regular finite-torsion local model; pointwise purity and composition used to compare the normalized curve with the ambient regular scheme. Input: Gabber purity for a regular Noetherian closed pair. More precisely: Expose XVI, section 3.7 second paragraph through its last paragraph, printed pp.254--255: semistable G-alteration, ell-Sylow H, tame equivariant modification, quotient over T=S prime/H, and log resolution. Geometric construction only, before applying Theorem 3.6.2 and Proposition 3.5.7; preliminary finite extension to normalize constants in the first paragraph. Specifically: XVI 3.7: scheme quotient X double-prime/H, projectivity over X, and the prime-to-ell generic cover. Supporting input: properness of the invariant Proj; ample twists and the finite projective-space embedding are obtained from existing nodes in the parent proof.
